clue.text: Something that can stop a car: a bikini during spring break, perhaps?

definitions.text: Something that can stop a car

parts.words: a bikini during spring break, perhaps
parts.note: spring break is classically spent in Florida, abbreviated Fla., and a bikini is beach attire

explanation.surface: A student in a skimpy swimsuit on a Florida beach makes drivers slam on the brakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'Fla. attire' (what you wear in Florida) runs together into FLAT TIRE. Spring break is the US college holiday, famously spent on Florida beaches.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctured, deflated tyre forces a driver to pull over, so it can bring a car to a halt.

clue.text: Fornicates (offers the ingredients needed for uncensored writing)

indicators.note: ingredients are raw materials, so the word before supplies the stock of letters to build from, with any of them usable more than once

parts.note: taken as written: its ten different letters are the whole stock
five of the same word's letters drawn on a second time, as a letter bank allows

explanation.surface: A cheeky note that sleeping around gives a writer material for unexpurgated prose.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a letter bank: FREE ASSOCIATION uses exactly the ten letters of FORNICATES, with E, A, S, O and I used twice, so it is not a strict anagram. The bracket makes Fornicates look like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Free association is the technique of writing down whatever comes to mind without self-censorship, as in Freudian analysis.

clue.text: Computer company's program topping the French

parts.note: an app is a software program
le is the masculine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: A tech firm's software outranks the French competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', and 'topping' just places the program first in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple is the American maker of the Mac and iPhone, a well-known computer company.

clue.text: Receptacle smelled nasty with the lid removed

indicators.note: removing a lid takes off the top, which in a down entry is the first letter

parts.note: stank is the past tense of stink

explanation.surface: A container gave off a foul smell once its lid was taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank is a large container for holding liquid or gas, so it is a receptacle.

clue.text: Mars moves quickly around center of Jupiter

indicators.note: around means the first word goes round the second, enclosing it

parts.note: to run is to move quickly

indicators.note: the center of a word is its middle letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters

explanation.surface: The planet Mars speeds round the core of Jupiter.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars looks like the planet, partnered with Jupiter, but it is a verb: to mar something is to spoil it.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or damage it, and to ruin it is the same in a stronger sense.

clue.text: Legal participant in California's capital, interrupting: "Am I American?"

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle of what follows, so it sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a capital is a head letter, so only the opening letter of the state's name is kept

parts.note: the first letter of California
US is short for American, as in US citizens

explanation.surface: Someone in Sacramento's courts asks, mid-hearing, whether they count as American.
explanation.walkthrough: AMICUS, as in amicus curiae, a friend of the court who offers a brief in a case without being a party to it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amicus curiae takes part in litigation by filing a brief, though not a party to the dispute.

clue.text: Trumpeter deceptively misleads (takes in) a couple of virtuosos

indicators.note: something presented deceptively is disguised, its letters rearranged to look like something else
takes in tells you the pair of letters is added to the scrambled word before the shuffle

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a couple means two, so just the opening pair of letters of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first two letters of virtuosos

explanation.surface: A jazz trumpeter fools a pair of virtuoso players.
explanation.definitionFit: Miles Davis was a jazz trumpeter and bandleader, famed for Kind of Blue.

clue.text: Worry cruelly tries someone determined to get ahead at all costs

definitions.text: someone determined to get ahead at all costs

parts.note: care is anxiety or worry

indicators.note: cruelly suggests something mangled or roughly treated, so these letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ruthless climber harshly frets over every attempt to get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A careerist puts personal advancement in their job above everything else, a ruthless climber.

clue.text: Vice president incorporates bits from comedians, some of them repeatedly

indicators.note: to incorporate bits from something is to build from its parts, so its letters are the raw stock rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: its nine different letters are the whole stock
the repeats: five of the comedians' letters used again, one of them twice more

explanation.surface: A vice president works borrowed jokes from comedians into speeches, some of them again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a letter bank: the answer uses exactly the nine letters of COMEDIANS, with C, O, D and M used twice and N three times.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice president is deputy to the president, the official next in rank who acts as the deputy commander.

clue.text: Behaves scornfully about last pair of Slovak shoes

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word encloses the selected letters

parts.note: to sneer is to behave with open scorn

indicators.note: last pair means only the final two letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the final two letters of Slovak

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs at a Slovak's footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneakers is the American word for soft rubber-soled sports shoes, called trainers in Britain.

clue.text: Former spouse criticizes particle growth

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
to pan a show is to criticize it harshly
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: An ex-partner sneers at someone's research into how particles grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Expansion is an increase in size or extent, a common synonym for growth.

clue.text: Singable excerpt from Joely Richardson

indicators.note: an excerpt is a piece lifted out of a longer text, so the letters sit inside the name

parts.note: the run of letters across the join of the first name and surname

explanation.surface: A tuneful passage taken from a performance by the actress Joely Richardson.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric as an adjective means suited to singing, as lyric poetry was once sung to the lyre.

clue.text: Murder victim is qualified to be heard

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken, so the word is matched by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: able means qualified or competent

explanation.surface: A detective remarks that the murdered person was well qualified, as everyone heard.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abel is killed by his brother Cain, the first murder in the Bible.

clue.text: Violinist playing 21

indicators.note: letters that are playing are moving about freely, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 21-across supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A violinist performing the piece numbered 21.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 and 21 are anagrams of each other, each clue pointing at the other; solve one and the other follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Stern was a celebrated American concert violinist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Roman officers reinterpret runic notes

indicators.note: to reinterpret is to read in a different way, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Officers of a legion puzzle over inscriptions carved in runes.
explanation.definitionFit: Centurions commanded a century, a company of about a hundred soldiers in the ancient Roman army.

clue.text: Ultimately, software bug limits overturning four-dimensional reality

indicators.note: something overturned is flipped end over end, so the string is read the other way
ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of software
a mite is a tiny bug
caps are upper limits, as on spending

explanation.surface: In the end a software glitch caps the overhaul of a physics simulation of four-dimensional reality.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics models the universe as spacetime, three spatial dimensions plus time fused into one continuum.

clue.text: Stepped down to thwart a bad edict

indicators.note: to thwart something is to knock it off course, so the letters are thrown out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ruler resigned rather than see a harmful decree blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who abdicates gives up the throne, which is to step down from power.

clue.text: Find unusual wrapper for unusual kind of radiation

indicators.note: a wrapper goes round its contents, enclosing them
unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters are put out of their ordinary order

parts.note: taken as written
rare means unusual

explanation.surface: A scientist hunts for strange packaging to shield a strange form of radiation.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'unusual' gives RARE; 'for' then places it inside the scrambled letters of 'Find'.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared is electromagnetic radiation just beyond visible red light, one kind among the spectrum's bands.

clue.text: Jumping bail, I could produce a defense

indicators.note: jumping letters leap about out of their order and land in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A suspect who skipped bail wonders what defense they could offer.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere when the crime happened, used as a defense in court.

clue.text: Military trainee acted without discipline

indicators.note: letters without discipline break ranks and fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young recruit misbehaved on parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training to become an officer in the armed forces.

clue.text: Authoritarian jerk following notes — yes, you read that correctly — backward

indicators.note: following says the jerk is placed after what precedes it, at the end of the answer

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale, so notes are fas

indicators.note: backward tells you the editorial note just before it is to be read from its end

parts.note: sic is the editor's mark saying a quotation is reproduced exactly as written
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: An editor flags that a writer really did call a bossy jerk 'backward' after the musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash-enclosed aside is not a comment on the clue but a piece of it: sic, written backward, sits between the notes and the jerk.
explanation.definitionFit: Fascistic describes rule by dictatorial force and suppression of opposition, an extreme form of authoritarianism.

clue.text: Discovers unlucky 13

indicators.note: unlucky suggests something that has gone wrong and been knocked into a jumble

parts.note: the answer to 13-across supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Someone finds out that thirteen is an unlucky number.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on thirteen being an unlucky number; 13 here is the answer to 13-across.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find something out for certain, so it is a synonym of discovers.

clue.text: Hogshead hidden in pleasant compartment

indicators.note: something hidden in another thing is tucked inside it

parts.note: nice means pleasant
split as hog's head, the head or first letter of hog

explanation.surface: A wine barrel is stowed away in a cosy little nook.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogshead looks like a big barrel, but split it into hog's head, the first letter of hog.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a recess or small compartment set into a wall or piece of furniture.

clue.text: Look over slide on mountain face

parts.note: to ski is to slide on snow

indicators.note: a face is the front, so only the leading letter of the word before it is kept

parts.note: the first letter of mountain

explanation.surface: A skier surveys a slope on a mountain face before heading down.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim a document is to read through it quickly, glancing over it rather than studying it.

clue.text: Poet takes in under $1,000

indicators.note: in a down entry, under places the second piece below the first one

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in a 50K salary
to take food in is to eat it

explanation.surface: A poet earns less than a thousand dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' places EATS below K in this down entry, rather than meaning less than.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was an English Romantic poet, author of the odes to a nightingale and autumn.

clue.text: Long tree

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to yearn for something
second meaning: a conifer with needles

explanation.walkthrough: Long here is a verb, as in long for home, not the adjective for length.
explanation.definitionFit: Pine is both a verb meaning to yearn sadly and the name of a common evergreen conifer.

clue.text: Paint romantic setting for prologue

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel inside it, so the letters are held within the words around

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A painter is told to depict a romantic scene as the opening of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro, short for introduction, is the opening part that comes before the main work, like a prologue.

clue.text: Ball of wax tangled lead chain

indicators.note: a tangled chain is twisted out of its proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lump of wax got caught up in a knotted chain made of lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole ball of wax and the whole enchilada are both American idioms for everything, so ball of wax and enchilada stand for each other.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US idioms 'the whole ball of wax' and 'the whole enchilada', the two nouns are interchangeable.

clue.text: Clothes-free enthusiast swallows insult

indicators.note: what swallows something takes it inside its body

parts.note: a nut is a fan or fanatic
to dis someone is to insult them

explanation.surface: A naturist shrugs off a jibe about going without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothes-free enthusiast is the definition as a whole; enthusiast is borrowed again for the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist practises going naked and is keen on the lifestyle, hence a clothes-free enthusiast.

clue.text: Discharged grass outside pastures

indicators.note: a word placed outside another wraps round it on both sides

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
leas are meadows or pastures

explanation.surface: Cattle let out of the barn are put to grass beyond the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: A discharged patient or prisoner is released, set free from a hospital or jail.
